chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abi Ali al-Khazzaz, from Dawud ibn Sulayman, who said:

I said to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him): I am afraid that something may happen and I will not be able to meet you, so inform me about the Imam after you? He said: My son, so-and-so, meaning Abul Hasan (peace be upon him).

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ: Abul Hasan (referring to Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida)
key_terms.إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Abraham (referring to Imam Musa ibn Ja'far, known as Abu Ibrahim)
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: The Imam (the divinely appointed successor and leader)

ai.seo_question: Who did Imam Musa al-Kadhim designate as his successor?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghay al-Ghayba*, Dawud ibn Sulayman seeks reassurance from Imam Musa al-Kadhim regarding the succession after his death, fearing he might miss the opportunity to meet the next Imam. The Imam explicitly identifies his son, Abul Hasan (Imam Ali al-Rida), thereby confirming the continuous line of Imamate within the progeny of Imam Husayn. This declaration is significant in Shia scholarship as it underscores the principle of *Nass* (explicit designation) and the divine appointment of Imams, reinforcing the legitimacy of the Twelfth Imam's eventual occultation.
